v.3: you are indeed one of the apostles,
v.5: [It is a scripture] sent down gradually from the All-mighty, the All-merciful
v.6: that you may warn a people whose fathers were not warned, so they are oblivious.
v.7: The word has certainly become due against most of them, so they will not have faith.
v.8: Indeed We have put iron collars around their necks, which are up to the chins, so their heads are upturned.
v.9: And We have put a barrier before them and a barrier behind them, then We have blind-folded them, so they do not see.
v.10: It is the same to them whether you warn them or do not warn them, they will not have faith.
v.11: You can only warn someone who follows the Reminder and fears the All-beneficent in secret; so give him the good news of forgiveness and a noble reward.
v.12: Indeed it is We who revive the dead and write what they have sent ahead and their effects [which they left behind], and We have figured everything in a manifest Imam.
v.13: Cite for them the example of the inhabitants of the town when the apostles came to it.
v.14: When We sent to them two [apostles], they impugned both of them. Then We reinforced them with a third, and they said, ‘We have indeed been sent to you.’
v.15: They said, ‘You are no other than human beings like us, and the All-beneficent has not sent down anything, and you are only lying.’
v.16: They said, ‘Our Lord knows that we have indeed been sent to you,
v.17: and our duty is only to communicate in clear terms.’
v.18: They said, ‘Indeed we take you for a bad omen. If you do not desist we will stone you, and surely a painful punishment will visit you from us.’
v.19: They said, ‘Your bad omens attend you. What! If you are admonished.... Indeed, you are an unrestrained lot.’
v.20: There came a man hurrying from the city outskirts. He said, ‘O my people! Follow the apostles!
v.21: Follow them who do not ask you any reward and they are rightly guided.
v.22: Why should I not worship Him who has originated me, and to whom you shall be brought back?
v.23: Shall I take gods besides Him? If the All-beneficent desired to cause me any distress, their intercession will not avail me in any way, nor will they rescue me.
v.24: Indeed, then I would be in manifest error.
v.25: Indeed I have faith in your Lord, so listen to me.’
v.26: He was told, ‘Enter paradise!’ He said, ‘Alas! Had my people only known
v.27: for what my Lord forgave me and made me one of the honoured ones!’
v.28: After him We did not send down on his people a host from the sky, nor We would have sent down.
v.29: It was but a single Cry, and, behold, they were stilled [like burnt ashes]!
v.30: How regrettable of the servants! There did not come to them any apostle but that they used to deride him.
v.31: Have they not regarded how many generations We have destroyed before them who will not come back to them?
v.32: And all of them will indeed be presented before Us.
v.33: A sign for them is the dead earth, which We revive and bring forth grain out of it, so they eat of it.
v.34: We make in it orchards of date palms and vines, and We cause springs to gush forth in it,
v.35: so that they may eat of its fruit and what their hands have cultivated. Will they not then give thanks?
v.36: Immaculate is He who has created all the kinds of what the earth grows, and of themselves, and of what they do not know.
v.37: A sign for them is the night, which We strip of daylight, and, behold, they find themselves in the dark!
v.38: The sun runs on to its place of rest: That is the ordaining of the All-mighty, the All-knowing.
v.39: As for the moon, We have ordained its phases, until it becomes like an old palm leaf.
v.40: Neither it behooves the sun to overtake the moon, nor may the night outrun the day, and each swims in an orbit.
v.41: A sign for them is that We carried their progeny in the laden ship,
v.42: and We have created for them what is similar to it, which they ride.
v.43: And if We like We drown them, whereat they have no one to call for help, nor are they rescued
v.44: except by a mercy from Us and for an enjoyment until some time.
v.45: And when they are told, ‘Beware of that which is before you and that which is behind you, so that you may receive [His] mercy…’
v.46: There does not come to them any sign from among the signs of their Lord but that they have been disregarding it.
v.47: When they are told, ‘Spend out of what Allah has provided you,’ the faithless say to the faithful, ‘Shall we feed [someone] whom Allah would feed, if He wished? You are only in manifest error.’
v.48: And they say, ‘When will this promise be fulfilled, should you be truthful?’
v.49: They do not await but a single Cry that will seize them as they wrangle.
v.50: Then they will not be able to make any will, nor will they return to their folks.
v.51: And when the Trumpet is blown, behold, there they will be, scrambling towards their Lord from their graves!
v.52: They will say, ‘Woe to us! Who raised us from our place of sleep?’ ‘This is what the All-beneficent had promised, and the apostles had spoken the truth!’
v.53: It will be but a single Cry, and, behold, they will all be presented before Us!
v.54: ‘Today no soul will be wronged in the least, nor will you be requited except for what you used to do.’
v.55: Indeed today the inhabitants of paradise rejoice in their engagements
v.56: —they and their mates, reclining on couches in the shades.
v.57: There they have fruits, and they have whatever they want.
v.59: And ‘Get apart today, you guilty ones!’
v.60: ‘Did I not exhort you, O children of Adam, saying, “Do not worship Satan. He is indeed your manifest enemy.
v.61: Worship Me. That is a straight path”?
v.62: Certainly, he has led astray many of your generations. Have you not exercised your reason?
v.63: This is the hell you had been promised!
v.64: Enter it today, because of what you used to deny.
v.65: Today We shall seal their mouths, and their hands shall speak to Us, and their feet shall bear witness concerning what they used to earn.’
v.66: Had We wished We would have blotted out their eyes: then, were they to advance towards the path, how would have they seen?
v.67: And had We wished We would have deformed them in their place; then they would neither have been able to move ahead nor to return.
v.68: And whomever We give a long life, We cause him to regress in creation. Then, will they not exercise their reason?
v.69: We did not teach him poetry, nor does it behoove him. This is just a reminder and a manifest Quran,
v.70: so that anyone who is alive may be warned, and that the word may come due against the faithless.
v.71: Have they not seen that We have created for them—of what Our hands have worked—cattle, so they have become their masters?
v.72: And We made them tractable for them; so some of them make their mounts and some of them they eat.
v.73: There are other benefits for them therein, and drinks. Will they not then give thanks?
v.74: They have taken gods besides Allah, [hoping] that they might be helped [by the fake deities].
v.75: [But] they cannot help them, while they [themselves] are an army mobilized for their defence.
v.76: So do not let their remarks grieve you. We indeed know whatever they hide and whatever they disclose.
v.77: Does not man see that We created him from a drop of [seminal] fluid, and, behold, he is an open contender!?
v.78: He draws comparisons for Us, and forgets his own creation. He says, ‘Who shall revive the bones when they have decayed?’
v.79: Say, ‘He will revive them who produced them the first time, and He has knowledge of all creation.
v.80: He, who made for you fire out of the green tree, and, behold, you light fire from it!
v.81: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the like of them? Yes indeed! He is the All-creator, the All-knowing.
v.82: All His command, when He wills something, is to say to it ‘Be,’ and it is.
v.83: So immaculate is He in whose hand is the dominion of all things, and to whom you shall be brought back.
